Experimental alpha.8 fixes **native Windows SSH agent routing**. Agent mode explicitly selects the standard Windows OpenSSH named pipe, so Git Bash/WSL/custom SSH_AUTH_SOCK values inherited from a terminal cannot redirect authentication. Linux continues to use its session agent socket. Explicit private-key mode disables the agent even when a valid identity is loaded.

Prepare/unlock your key in your OS agent before selecting SSH agent in Repo Stealer. The application does not start/configure the Windows service or add/remove/export agent keys. Host-key discovery remains unauthenticated: independently verify the fingerprint before approving capture. Strict per-job host pinning, isolated SSH configuration, disabled forwarding/password prompts, encrypted staging and no-overwrite publication remain mandatory. See [Windows agent setup](https://github.com/hrishi072/repo-stealer/blob/main/docs/DESKTOP.md#windows-native-agent-setup).

Native Linux/Windows CLI and WebKitGTK/WebView2 tests cover agent-only full-history capture and offline restore with the original synthetic private-key path unavailable, wrong/changed host rejection before authentication, missing/unloaded identities, duplicate-name refusal, private-key-mode isolation, timeout/cancellation cleanup and no failed snapshot publication. Windows additionally covers an invalid inherited socket and a stopped native service. Only disposable GitHub-hosted Windows test runners temporarily change their agent service; fixture cleanup removes only generated identities and restores original service settings and baseline keys. Linux tests use a separate isolated agent. Existing native storage, Git/HTTPS/LFS/provider/history, browser, package and reciprocal recovery gates remain required.

Alpha.8 retains alpha.7's SSH Git-history capture, guided Linux LUKS/Windows EFS setup, repository cards/snapshot picker, encrypted migration history and read-only reconciliation, bounded four-worker LFS transfers and cancellable provider/LFS HTTP waits. Local/HTTPS Git and optional LFS capture, offline restore and same-key portable backups remain supported. SSH capture archives Git history only; use HTTPS to include LFS payloads. The source SSH key, agent endpoint and trust configuration are not archived. Existing destinations remain protected; no synchronization, automatic retry/resume, rollback or adoption is added.

Vault, snapshot and backup formats are unchanged. SSH-origin snapshots require alpha.7 or newer; LFS manifest v3 requires alpha.6 or newer; existing local v1 and HTTPS-origin v2 remain readable. Same-key recovery still needs the original vault passphrase; there is no password reset. No hosting token is persisted in plans, archives, backups, preferences or activity. Lock clears decrypted metadata.

Guarded migration creates only new private personal repositories on GitHub/GitLab cloud/self-hosted instances, using SHA-1 snapshots with an existing symbolic default branch, at most 128 heads/tags and 8 KiB ref-name bytes. GitHub requires classic repo+workflow scopes; GitLab requires personal api+write_repository. Identity/policy checks, disabled destination automation, exact atomic ref leases and independent Git/LFS verification remain mandatory. Incomplete operations can leave a new private repository and partial data; inspect encrypted receipts instead of replaying a consumed plan. Organization/group creation, existing-repository writes, SSH migration destinations, hosting issues/PR metadata and external submodule transfer remain unsupported.

LFS support requires canonical three-line SHA-256 v1 pointers, at most 10,000 objects, 10 GiB per object and 100 GiB total. Streaming uses batches of up to 100 objects and one to four workers. Redirects, automatic retries, SSH LFS, custom adapters/tus/proxies, nonstandard discovery and pointer extensions are unsupported. Queued objects stop on worker failure and started workers join before cleanup. OS filesystem/name-resolution work remains outside a strict cancellation-latency guarantee.

Installed Git 2.48+ and verified encrypted Git working storage are required: ext4/XFS on mounted LUKS for Linux, EFS for Windows. Linux desktop requires writable /dev/shm tmpfs for its private browser profile; Windows uses incognito WebView2. OS swap/dump policy is separate.

Choose **repo-stealer-desktop-*** for graphical installers: Linux x86_64 DEB/RPM/AppImage or Windows x86_64 NSIS setup EXE. The other six packages are the CLI. SHA256SUMS is included. Source commits and version tags are SSH-signed; installers are not OS code-signed. Installed DEB/NSIS and extracted AppImage launch/version checks gate publication. Desktop RPM packaging/digests are checked; Fedora/openSUSE desktop RPM installation remains untested.

This is an experimental application without independent application security review. Read [SSH capture](https://github.com/hrishi072/repo-stealer/blob/main/docs/REMOTE-CAPTURE.md#ssh-capture), [LFS scope](https://github.com/hrishi072/repo-stealer/blob/main/docs/GIT-LFS.md) and [guarded migrations](https://github.com/hrishi072/repo-stealer/blob/main/docs/GUARDED-MIGRATIONS.md) for supported credentials, administrative-race boundaries and recovery instructions. Keep a verified encrypted backup.
